reason: The passage clearly emphasizes hierarchical relationships, most notably in the demonstration of Moses' authoritative leadership over the Levites. When Moses commands the Levites to execute divine judgment (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה), they obey without question (וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ לֵוִ֖י כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה - 'the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses'). The narrative structure repeatedly underscores Moses' special role as the one who led the people out of Egypt and his supreme authority in interpreting God's will. Aaron also initially functions as a leader figure when Moses is absent, though his actions are portrayed negatively. The emphasis is on obedience to hierarchical authority and proper chain of command.
